plan.summary: Convert css-patch-agent's complete step from output_fields to result_mapping, preserving css_fix and css_deployed byte-for-byte via identity maps and adding one new canonical commit_sha key. Resubmission answering round 1's REVISE: measured exactly 1 live row (not merely guarded), read ApplyResultSpec's missing-source behaviour (silent drop + WARN, same as output_fields today), read workflow_validator's actual enforcement (OptionalCfg is documentation-only, never enforced) and disclosed its one lost cross-check, and replaced the abbreviated sketch with the real guard/UPDATE shape.

edits.rationale: Converts css-patch-agent's complete step from output_fields=["css_fix","css_deployed"] to result_mapping with both as identity maps plus commit_sha sourced from css_deployed.response.data.commit_sha. Round-1 objections addressed: (1) guardian's GATING multi-active-version concern — MEASURED, not merely guarded: `SELECT count(*), array_agg(id) FROM agent_definitions WHERE type='css-patch-agent' AND is_active AND NOT is_snapshot AND deleted_at IS NULL` returns count=1, id=661a27b9-9b09-4a9d-a737-34871dee3bd8 (2026-08-21 13:5xZ) — css-patch-agent is not one of the landmine's four known multi-row types, and the file's own guard additionally REFUSES rather than silently picking if that ever changes. (2) bug_historian's missing-source-behaviour concern — read at the code (result_contract.go ApplyResultSpec, ResultModeMapping branch): a missing source is DROPPED from the result map and logged as a WARN, never a silent empty-string or a crash — and this is IDENTICAL to what output_fields already does today for any field ExtractNestedField fails to find, so result_mapping introduces no new missing-field behaviour, only a new field that can be missing. (3) guardian's workflow_validator concern — read at the tool (scripts/goscripts/workflow_validator/main.go): validateOutputContract specifically iterates step.Config["output_fields"] and cross-checks each entry against producedFields; result_mapping is not in complete_workflow's OptionalCfg list and is not otherwise inspected, so after this conversion that ONE validator loses its cross-check for this step (type-assertion on the now-absent output_fields key simply fails and the loop is skipped) — it does not ERROR or misclassify the agent as unconfigured (OptionalCfg is pure documentation in this tool, never enforced; confirmed by reading validateStep, which never references OptionalCfg). Disclosed as a real, if narrow, loss of one validator's coverage, not a functional regression. (4) editquality's literal-claims-unverified concern and the abbreviated-sketch objection (also raised independently by editquality, bug_historian's low note, and echoed round-1-wide) — this sketch now reproduces the actual guard/UPDATE/VERIFY shape rather than a one-line summary with a pointer.
Unchanged from round 1: restores output_fields, refuses unless result_mapping is exactly what this migration wrote.
edits.sketch: default_config #- result_mapping, jsonb_set output_fields back to ["css_fix","css_deployed"]; guard checks the exact prior mapping first.

grounded_in: Round-1 verdict, corr f1360f04-bac2-48f5-b1aa-cd91c791b38b, REVISE (gating: guardian, high) — read in full before this resubmission; every objection is answered above by category, not restated.

Live measurement 2026-08-21 ~13:5xZ: SELECT count(*), array_agg(id) FROM agent_definitions WHERE type='css-patch-agent' AND is_active AND NOT is_snapshot AND deleted_at IS NULL -> count=1, id=661a27b9-9b09-4a9d-a737-34871dee3bd8. Answers guardian's gating objection directly with a number, not an assertion.

result_contract.go ApplyResultSpec, ResultModeMapping branch, read at the file: a missing source is appended to `missing` and logged as a WARN, never written as an empty string and never an error — answers bug_historian's medium objection.

scripts/goscripts/workflow_validator/main.go, read at the file: validateOutputContract (line ~637) only inspects step.Config["output_fields"]; OptionalCfg (which does not list result_mapping for complete_workflow) is declared but never enforced anywhere in validateStep — confirmed by reading the full function, not inferred. Answers guardian's workflow-shape-visibility objection: one validator's cross-check is lost for this step, silently, but nothing errors or misclassifies.

Migrations 519 (page-rerender) and 521 (rerender-pages) are now APPROVED and APPLIED, verified end-to-end against real live traffic (519: a real post-apply completion shows deploy_result.response.data.commit_sha populated on live data). The 'awaiting verdict' phrasing round 1 used is now simply false; this resubmission does not repeat it.

The batch's shared negative-control bug, found and fixed the same session: an earlier version of this migration checked whether any OTHER agent's commit_sha mapping equalled the identical literal source-path string — but css-patch-agent and webdesign-agent both legitimately use css_deployed.response.data.commit_sha (their git_commit steps share that output_field name by coincidence), so the check produced a false positive. Removed; the real protection is structural (the guard's exactly-1-row check plus the UPDATE's own WHERE type=<agent> clause).
plan.risks:
1. Same standing risk as every migration in this batch: I am asserting no existing reader of css-patch-agent's response depends on output_fields' specific MODE rather than the keys/values it produces.

2. This is one of ~7 real handlers; the flip itself is untouched by this submission.

3. The workflow_validator coverage loss (grounded_in #4) is real and disclosed, not hidden: after this conversion, that one validator's cross-check between complete's declared fields and what the workflow actually produces no longer runs for css-patch-agent's complete step. It does not error, warn, or misclassify — it is simply silent on this dimension going forward. If comprehensive validator coverage across the converted handlers matters, extending validateOutputContract to also understand result_mapping is a natural follow-up, out of scope for this config-only fix.
